events.title: First working Lisp interpreter
events.summary: By May 1959, McCarthy's Lisp implementation at MIT had become a serious, usable interpreter on the IBM 704.
events.about: Lisp was built for AI and symbolic computing — programs as nested lists, recursion, and eval. Early uses: theorem proving, language experiments, and research tools. Later it influenced Emacs, CAD systems, and languages from Python to Clojure.

narrative.whyChosen: Lisp introduced symbolic expression programming and ideas that later shaped AI, Emacs, and functional languages.
narrative.whyImportant: It established list processing, recursion, and eval-based semantics as a practical computing model.
narrative.problemSolved: Researchers needed a language for symbolic reasoning and AI experiments beyond numeric FORTRAN-style code.
